text: The task set and the timer set of a route are governed rows with a version, read for the approved route through rwb-decision. The step composes the to state, the task codes and the timer types and values from that row, records them with the version applied, and asserts no code, no duration and no default: the sets, their codes and their values stay open as CG-B2-S1-012-1 until their owner publishes them, and the contract declares the elements with their source and no value. The element set of the route-start answer inside Approval is declared from the requirements (REQ-S1-007) and carries the placeholder where the source is silent.
why: The legacy story and FSD S1 A2.12 open the chosen route, create its tasks and start its clocks, BR-S1-012 forbids writing a business value in code, and no read source publishes the task set, the timer set, their codes or their values.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-012 Data table (task, timer, DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-036); FSD S1 A2.12.1, A2.12.3.1 BR-S1-012 and A2.12.3.3; TSD S1 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-01, R-SET-01, R-DIL-01 and R-LIT-01 with their timer column; Template and Rules §R5.5 and §R9
confirm: Owner of the route sets in rwb-decision with the business owner of module S1, before the wave 3 contract tag
impact: If the sets are published as rows of a route table rather than as elements of the rule answer, the read row and the record element keep their shape and only the owner's answer changes; the start behaviour is unchanged

text: The four consumed rows are read on the operation each owner publishes, and until that name is published the clients are built against the documented use and their fakes. rwb-case answers the case state and the route-start answer and owns the recovery_case, task and timer rows, which it creates from the answered sets; rwb-decision answers the rule row in force and the governed sets; rwb-access answers the authorise check. Each is one hop with a 2 s budget and no chain, and the route start travels on the case answer and not on an event of this service.
why: No source publishes the operation names of the consumed rows, no source says which service owns the task and timer rows after the split, and the plan rows of both stories carry no class C dependency, so the stories must be buildable on Day 1 against a documented use and a fake.
read: Context pack S1 ownership rows (no table, no event, no job); TSD S1 T3.1, T3.3, T5.1 and T5.2; FSD S1 A2.12.2; legacy RWB-E4-012 Data table; Template and Rules §R5.4 and §R5.5 DP-11
confirm: Owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access at the wave 3 tag
impact: A published name is an additive minor version of the baseline and a client change; if rwb-case refuses the task and timer sets, the owning service and its contract are named and the sets move with them, and the case states are unchanged

text: No S1 rule package is in force for the route-start step. The step reads whatever rule id and rule version the rwb-decision answer carries for the business date and the approved route, applies that row's action, to state and timer, and applies no local decision table of its own; if the answer carries no rule id, the record carries the placeholder and the version of the decision answer, never an invented rule id.
why: Both legacy criteria require the result to be recorded with the rule version, and no source publishes an S1 route-start rule, its parameter or its row.
read: FSD S1 A2.12.3.1 BR-S1-012 and A2.12.4.1; TSD S1 T3.2 and T8; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-01, R-SET-01, R-DIL-01 and R-LIT-01; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-04 context
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision with the business owner of module S1 before the S1 package is promoted
impact: A published rule id and version fill the same element with no behavioural change; a rule parameter would move the sets to the rule answer and keep the record shape

why: The overlay for D-RCV-60 records a missing approval or status as an assumption and continues at Draft rather than stopping the run.

confirm: Business lead and solution architect, S1, at the next review point
